name: Armadale Reptile Centre
reason: Rule 1-2: Tourism WA attraction listing (westernaustralia.com/en/attraction/armadale-reptile-centre) and Experience Perth Hills '10 must-visit nature and wildlife experiences' both name it; open six days with paid entry, 50+ reptile species plus kangaroos and dingoes, a 1-2 hr visit.
objection: A small suburban wildlife centre (786 views); friend test says 'only if nearby with kids'. Closed Wednesdays outside school holidays.

name: Kanyana Wildlife Rehabilitation Centre
reason: For: Experience Perth Hills names it among the hills' 10 must-visit wildlife experiences (Discovery Tours, nocturnal tours; bilbies and woylies); Destination Perth listed it. Against rule 2: it is a working wildlife hospital visitors can enter only on booked tours on Thursdays and Sundays, not whenever they arrive.
objection: Tour-only access two days a week, bookings essential; one counted source for a marginal place.

name: Perth's Outback Splash
reason: Rule 1-2, 4: Tourism WA attraction listing ('one of WA's top outdoor entertainment destinations') and the Swan Valley tourism listing name it; a water park with 9 slides, mazes and mini-golf, a half-day visit. Seasonal venue (Sept-April), which rule 4 allows.
objection: A family amusement venue mainly for locals' children; closed May-August since 2024.

name: Ocean Reef Marina
reason: Rule 1-2: no visitor source names it; it is a boat marina still under development (the coastal pool and beach were due to open in 2026, not confirmed open). A marina is a local facility, not a visitor draw today.
objection: Government expects it to become a 'key attraction like Hillarys Boat Harbour' once the pool opens; re-look when it does.

name: Sunset Heritage Precinct
reason: Rule 1-2: no visitor source; the former Sunset Hospital site has 'remained largely unused since 1995', with only open grounds and picnic facilities, and the state is seeking redevelopment proposals (EOI closed Aug 2026).
objection: 2903 page views and riverside grounds open since 2016; if redeveloped as an arts/cultural precinct it could qualify later.

name: Sunset Coast
reason: Rule 3: a tourism-brand stretch of coastline (Perth's northern beaches), not a single place; its beaches (Cottesloe, Scarborough, Trigg etc.) are judged as candidates in their own right. No counted source names it as somewhere to go as one spot.
objection: The name does appear in Perth tourism marketing; it could serve as name evidence for a coast grouping, but not as a pinned spot.

name: Sikh Heritage Cremation Site
reason: Rule 3: a minor heritage marker on the Australian Sikh Heritage Trail; no visitor source, 0 views, nothing to do for half an hour.
objection: Culturally significant to a community heritage trail.

name: Mundaring Sculpture Park
reason: Rule 1-2: Tourism WA attraction listing (Mundaring Community Sculpture Park: sculptures by eight WA artists, the Moodae-ring acoustic sculpture) and Experience Perth Hills town guides name it; sculpture walk, playground, trailhead of the Munda Biddi and Railway Reserves Heritage Trails. Name in the app should be 'Mundaring Community Sculpture Park'.
objection: Essentially a small town park with a playground; the Saturday farmers' market there is not part of the spot (rule 4). Could be argued a local park (review).

name: Wyola Wreck
reason: Rule 1-3: no counted source as a visitor place; the stern frame of a tug buried in the sand at CY O'Connor Beach, North Coogee, plus a shallow dive site in the WA Museum's wreck notes. A short look or a specialist dive, not a general draw.
objection: WA Museum (an agency) documents it as a shallow dive with marine growth; a quirky beach relic that could support a CY O'Connor Beach spot's bio.

name: Bell Cottage Ruin
reason: Rule 2: the state heritage entry says the ruin is fenced, inaccessible to the public and obscured from view by trees; heritage register only, no visitor source.
objection: State Register-listed, part of the East Rockingham Heritage Precinct.

name: Samuel Ferguson's Cottage
reason: Rule 1-3: only Wikipedia/heritage listings; a cottage (ruin) that is one numbered stop on the Toodyay Pioneer Heritage Trail, a minor part of a larger walk with nothing to do for half an hour.
objection: It is a named stop of a heritage trail, which can qualify a heritage building; but the trail is the draw, not this ruin.

name: Mahogany Inn
reason: Brief rule: accommodation venue (a historic inn operating as a B&B/function venue); no visitor source names it as a sight.
objection: Historic 1840s inn building in the Perth Hills.

name: Redemptorist Monastery
reason: Rule 1-2 (church rule): a working monastery and church in North Perth; no visitor source names anything to see or do there (no interior tour, art or guide mention). Heritage register and Wikipedia only.
objection: 1517 page views; an imposing heritage building, but only seen from the street as far as any source says.

name: Kuljak Island
reason: Rule 1-3: an artificial island on a capped former rubbish tip off Ascot Waters with footpaths; no visitor source (the Swan River kangaroo island visitors go to is Heirisson Island, a different place downstream). A local riverside reserve.
objection: Has walking paths and is a backdrop to Peninsula Farm (Tranby House) across the river.

name: E Shed Markets
reason: Rule 4: a market that trades only Friday to Sunday (and public holidays), not daily.
objection: Wikivoyage mentions it in passing near the Rottnest ferry wharf; it is a fixed venue at Victoria Quay.

name: Peninsula Farm
reason: For: the National Trust heritage house and farm (formerly Tranby House, now 'Peninsula Farm at Wu-rut Woorat', 1839) on the Swan River; Hello Perth visitor guide names it, the house is open with volunteer guides and an entry fee, the grounds daily, with a cafe. Likely the same place as any 'Tranby House' candidate: keep as one under its current name.
objection: The house opens only Friday and Saturday; one visitor source; a suburban heritage house museum, 'only if nearby'.

name: Perth Hills
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage district 'Perth/The Hills' and the Experience Perth Hills tourism brand name it; it is a region (John Forrest NP, Mundaring Weir, Lesmurdie Falls, Kalamunda) — name evidence for the proposer (a destination or grouping), not a single pinned spot.
objection: An area, not a place: it cannot be a spot itself; the proposer must decide whether it is a destination or whether its parts are Perth spots.

name: WA Shipwrecks Museum
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Fremantle See listing, Visit Fremantle top free things and Tourism WA's Fremantle page all name it; free museum with the Batavia timbers, 1-2 hr visit.
objection: Weak score only because it has no article of its own under this title (Wikipedia: 'Western Australian Shipwrecks Museum'); none on substance.

name: Western Australian Maritime Museum
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Fremantle See listing and Tourism WA's Fremantle page; museum with Australia II and the HMAS Ovens submarine tour, open daily.
objection: None of substance; 0 views is a title mismatch with its Wikipedia article.

name: HMAS Ovens
reason: Rule 3: duplicate/part of the Western Australian Maritime Museum: the submarine is toured as part of a museum ticket on Victoria Quay; keep it as one with the museum and mention it in the museum's bio.
objection: 4800 page views and a separate tour ticket; a vessel-as-attraction could stand alone, but it sits beside the museum and is sold with it.

name: Round House
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Fremantle See listing and Visit Fremantle's top free things; WA's oldest public building (1831), a free small museum on Arthur Head with views over Bathers Bay.
objection: A short visit (30 min) on a small headland; strong enough with two sources.

name: Whalers' Tunnel
reason: Rule 3: part of the Round House (it runs under it on Arthur Head to Bathers Beach); keep as one with the Round House and mention the tunnel in its bio.
objection: Wikivoyage gives it its own See listing as a self-guided display.

name: Cantonment Hill
reason: For: Wikivoyage Fremantle See listing ('a terrific view of Fremantle Harbour'), free lookout beside the Army Museum. Against: one counted source and a short viewpoint visit; the signal station building is not open; Visit Fremantle points visitors to Monument Hill instead.
objection: Marginal per the one-source-and-short-visit rule; may be best mentioned in the Army Museum's bio.

name: Army Museum of Western Australia
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Fremantle See listing with hours and prices; a military museum in the old Artillery Barracks, 1-2 hr visit.
objection: Opens only Wed-Fri and Sun, 10:30-3; one counted source.

name: The Moores Building
reason: For: Wikivoyage Do listing: a contemporary art gallery with six exhibition spaces in the West End, free entry. Against rule 3: Wikivoyage itself calls it part of Fremantle Arts Centre; a small gallery whose shows come and go.
objection: Part-of signal: if Fremantle Arts Centre is kept, this is a near-duplicate; could also be folded into the West End spot.

name: Bathers Beach
reason: Rule 1-2: Visit Fremantle top free things (Manjaree / Bathers Beach) and Tourism WA's Fremantle page name it; a swimming beach below the Round House with a licensed area on the sand and the Bathers Beach art precinct.
objection: Small town beach; near-duplicate risk with the Round House/Fishing Boat Harbour precinct.

name: South Beach
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Fremantle Do listing and Visit Fremantle's free things ('much-loved' family swimming beach with BBQs, shade, sauna). NOTE: the candidate's coordinates (25.78, -80.14) are South Beach, Miami: the pin must be re-resolved in South Fremantle (about -32.076, 115.751 per Wikivoyage).
objection: A suburban family beach; second tier.

name: Fisherman's Wharf
reason: Rule 1-2: keep as 'Fishing Boat Harbour' (Fremantle Fishing Boat Harbour), the place Visit Fremantle (top 10 free, #9), Tourism WA's Fremantle page and Wikivoyage ('Esplanade and Boat harbour') name: boardwalks, working fishing fleet, the Bon Scott statue, fish and chips. 'Fisherman's Wharf' is only Cicerello's outdoor seating there.
objection: Partly a dining strip (rule: restaurants alone fail); the Bon Scott statue and boardwalk carry it.

name: Cappuccino Strip
reason: For: Fremantle's famous cafe street (South Terrace), named by Wikivoyage (walking area), Visit Fremantle ('the famous Cappuccino Strip', a stop on the Fremantle Discovery Trail) and Tourism WA. Against rule 2: it is a strip of cafes and restaurants; a street of businesses, which the bar fails unless the street itself is the recognised attraction.
objection: Could be judged a recognised landmark street (keep) or folded into a Fremantle town/West End spot.

name: Fremantle West End
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage ('West End' walking area), Visit Fremantle (heritage-listed West End, galleries, Discovery Trail) and Tourism WA name it: Australia's largest intact Victorian-era port streetscape, walked for an hour or more.
objection: A district rather than a single place; overlaps the Round House, Shipwrecks Museum and Moores Building it contains. If Fremantle itself is a destination, the proposer may fold it into the description.

name: Esplanade Park, Fremantle
reason: For: Tourism WA's Fremantle page (Ferris wheel at Esplanade Park) and Visit Fremantle (Esplanade Reserve on the Discovery Trail, skate park, playground). Against rule 3 / Leave out: an urban park under Norfolk pines whose draws are a seasonal-ish tourist wheel and a youth skate park; 'an ordinary park' negative benchmark.
objection: Two counted sources name it, but as a place to pass through on the way to the Fishing Boat Harbour.

name: Fremantle Walking Tours and Trails
reason: A spot is a place: a set of tours and self-guided trails, not a place; the places they visit (West End, Round House, Prison) are their own candidates.
objection: Visit Fremantle promotes the Discovery Trail; it belongs in Fremantle's tips.

name: Rottnest Island
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage park page and Tourism WA's Rottnest Island page; car-free island reserve with quokkas, beaches and snorkelling, Perth's top day trip (81,891 views). Area: the proposer decides destination vs spot.
objection: None on inclusion; only the destination-vs-spot question.

name: Wadjemup Lighthouse
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Rottnest See listing; stop on every island tour (Rottnest Express Grand Island Tour), on the island's highest point with views; lighthouse tours run by the island authority.
objection: Operators say you can't always enter; a short stop. Part of the island, but a distinct named sight.

name: The Basin
reason: Rule 1-2: Rottnest's best-known swimming beach: the Rottnest Island Authority's beach guide (rottnestisland.com, blocked to scripts) and the ferry operators' guides rank it first; patrolled in summer, shallow reef pool. Second-tier beach a source names: keep.
objection: No unblocked counted source opened (rottnestisland.com returns a bot wall; Wikivoyage Rottnest names beaches only generally); check the RIA page in a browser.

name: Cathedral Rocks
reason: Rule 1-2: purpose-built viewing platform over a New Zealand fur seal colony at Rottnest's West End, a stop on island tours (Rottnest Express Grand Island Tour, opened) and in Rottnest Island Authority material. NOTE: the candidate's coordinates (-77.85, 162.6) are Cathedral Rocks, Antarctica: re-resolve near Cape Vlamingh (about -32.02, 115.45).
objection: Short look (15-30 min) and the second counted source is an operator; could be folded into a West End/Cape Vlamingh spot.

name: Armstrong Bay
reason: For: (Little) Armstrong Bay is repeatedly named by Rottnest guides as one of the island's best beginner snorkelling bays. Against: sources found are ferry operators, not counted; one of dozens of Rottnest bays; the candidate is 'Armstrong Bay' while guides name 'Little Armstrong Bay'.
objection: Rottnest has 60+ bays; listing many dilutes the island; one beach spot (The Basin) may suffice.

name: Thomson Bay
reason: For: the island's main settlement where the ferries land, with the shops, bakery, museum and accommodation; visitors base there (town rule). Against rule 3: it is the arrival point of Rottnest Island rather than a separate draw, and no counted source names it as somewhere to go in itself.
objection: Likely a near-duplicate of Rottnest Island; useful only if the island becomes a destination with the settlement as its gateway spot.

name: Oliver Hill Battery
reason: Rule 1-2: Wikivoyage Rottnest See ('wartime remnants, such as old barracks and cannons') and the island's guided Oliver Hill guns-and-tunnels tour (Rottnest Express Grand Island Tour, opened): restored 9.2-inch WWII guns and tunnels, a 45-60 min tour, reached by the heritage train.
objection: Tour-led access; the second counted source is an operator, the authority's own page was bot-blocked.

name: Rottnest Quokkas
reason: A spot is a place / rule 3: the quokkas live across the whole island; they are Rottnest Island's draw, not a separate place. Duplicate of Rottnest Island (mention in its bio).
objection: The quokka is the island's headline experience; but there is no single place to pin.

name: Swan Valley
reason: Rule 1: Wikivoyage district 'Perth/Swan_Valley', Wikivoyage Perth and Tourism WA (Swan Valley under Perth and Surrounds); wine, brewery and food region. Area: name evidence for the proposer (destination or spot).
objection: An area, not a single place; the proposer decides.

name: Guildford
reason: Town rule: Wikivoyage Swan Valley See listing ('one of WA's oldest settlements', whole town a heritage locality, James St) and Perth page (antique stores); the gateway to the Swan Valley.
objection: A suburb now absorbed into Perth; its draw is a heritage streetscape, a 1-2 hr wander.

name: Swan Valley Visitor Centre
reason: Rule 2: a visitor information centre, not an attraction; the museum it is attached to (Guildford courthouse/gaol) would be judged on its own.
objection: Wikivoyage gives it a See listing and notes the attached museum.

name: All Saints Anglican Church, Henley Brook
reason: For: Wikivoyage Swan Valley See listing names it as Western Australia's oldest church (1841) with a historic cemetery, grounds and a walk to the Swan River; entry free (church rule: a landmark a guide singles out). Against: one counted source and a short visit; still a working parish church.
objection: One source plus a 20-30 minute stop; marginal by rule.

name: Houghtons Wines
reason: Brief winery rule: the Houghton name has left the Swan Valley — the winery was sold to Oakover in 2019 and the site is now Nikola Estate; Wikivoyage's link is marked dead. Under this name it is not a place to go.
objection: The 1836 estate is WA's oldest winery; if the owner wants it, judge 'Nikola Estate' as its own candidate (a landmark estate could qualify).

name: Oakover Wines
reason: Brief winery rule: one of dozens of Swan Valley cellar doors in a bare Wikivoyage list, no source singles it out as a destination.
objection: Large family estate with restaurant; but no guide singles it out.

name: Jarrah Ridge
reason: Brief winery rule: a cellar door in a bare Wikivoyage list, not singled out as a destination.
objection: None beyond the list mention.

name: Sitella Wines
reason: Brief winery rule: a cellar door in a bare Wikivoyage list, not singled out as a destination.
objection: None beyond the list mention.

name: Talijancich
reason: Brief winery rule: a cellar door in a bare Wikivoyage list, not singled out as a destination.
objection: Known for fortified wines; still one of dozens.

name: Carilley Estate
reason: Brief winery rule: a cellar door in a bare Wikivoyage list, not singled out as a destination.
objection: None beyond the list mention.

name: The Olive Farm
reason: Brief winery rule: a cellar door/farm shop in a bare Wikivoyage list, not singled out as a destination.
objection: None beyond the list mention.

name: Feral Brewing
reason: Brief brewery rule: a brewery taproom in a bare Wikivoyage list; no source singles it out as a destination in its own right.
objection: A well-known craft brewery among beer travellers; still a bar/restaurant venue.

name: Lancaster Wines
reason: Brief winery rule: a cellar door in a bare Wikivoyage list, not singled out as a destination.
objection: None beyond the list mention.

name: Garbin Estate
reason: Brief winery rule: a cellar door in a bare Wikivoyage list, not singled out as a destination.
objection: None beyond the list mention.

name: Jane Brook Estate
reason: Brief winery rule: a cellar door in a bare Wikivoyage list, not singled out as a destination.
objection: None beyond the list mention.

name: Edgecombe Wines
reason: Brief winery rule: a family cafe and cellar door (Wikivoyage Eat listing 'Edgecombe Brothers'); no source singles it out as a destination.
objection: Wikivoyage gives it an Eat entry, i.e. a restaurant.

name: Henley Park
reason: Brief winery rule: a cellar door in a bare Wikivoyage list, not singled out as a destination. (Candidate coordinates are Henley Park in England.)
objection: None beyond the list mention.
